_comment: The fleet's auto-mode classifier configuration (agent-fabric ADR-008), written into every login's ~/.claude/settings.json by runtime/claude-code/user-settings.py. `environment` maps a slot of Claude Code's own environment list (`claude auto-mode defaults`) to the fleet's text for it: each named slot replaces the built-in entry of that name, every other built-in entry is kept as Claude Code words it, and a slot Claude Code does not have is added. A replaced slot carries over any safeguard its built-in text states, since replacing drops it. `allow`, `soft_deny` and `hard_deny` are added to the built-in lists ("$defaults" first), never replacing them. Every entry is prose the classifier reads as a rule: state facts and boundaries, never a regex, and nothing broader than what is true — the classifier trusts what this says. A fact here must be true of every agent on every host; what one project needs belongs in that project's own rules. Keep it short — the classifier reads all of it on every decision.

environment.Organization: BlueTeam-OU and gzapi-org on GitHub: one owner operating a fleet of AI agents. The fabric's own repositories (agent-fabric, agent-fabric-gateway) are under BlueTeam-OU; the gzapi client's are under gzapi-org. Each agent is a Linux login with its own role (fabric-status names it), coordinated by agent-fabric (github.com/BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric), which every agent reads and only the fabric-coordinator role writes.
environment.Primary use of Claude Code: software development on the fleet's projects: agents edit code, run tests, commit, push their own branches (named <host>/<login>/<type>/<what>), open, review and merge pull requests with the gh CLI, and message each other over GZCoord.
environment.Repository visibility: PUBLIC: BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric and gzapi-org/InterWeave — a push to either publishes to the world. INTERNAL: BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric-gateway. PRIVATE: gzapi-org/gzapp, gzapi-org/gzapp.decks, gzapi-org/gzapi.brand, gzapi-org/gzapi.ge, BlueTeam-OU/blueteam.ee, andreabenetton/kutaisi-shop-transit, and each gzapi-org/agent-fabric-secrets-<id> (one encrypted secrets store per agent). Confidential material may go only to a private repo; a secret value goes to no repo except, encrypted, through fabric-secrets into an agent's secrets store. Any other repository is private only if the remote host and repo name indicate it or a visibility check in the transcript shows it; a meta line reading `"visibility":"unverified"` means org policy barred the harness from checking — treat that repo as possibly public: scope what is OK to commit or push there as for a public repo, and Out-of-Place Publication applies to it as to a known-public destination.
environment.Source control: exactly the repositories named under Repository visibility, on github.com, and no others: a repository not named there — including one created in the session, in gzapi-org or anywhere — is outside the trust boundary. github.com/andreabenetton/gzapi.ge and andreabenetton/gzapp.decks are older names GitHub redirects to the gzapi-org repos; andreabenetton/kutaisi-shop-transit is that project's only remote. Agents push their own branches and merge through pull requests. main is protected by GitHub only on gzapi-org/gzapp and gzapi-org/InterWeave: on every other repo, nothing on the server refuses a direct or force push to main, so the agent must not make one.
environment.Org-specific CLIs: the fabric's commands in ~/.local/bin — fabric-accounts, fabric-adr, fabric-branches, fabric-ctl, fabric-fresh, fabric-host, fabric-jobs, fabric-lease, fabric-locale, fabric-model, fabric-results, fabric-review, fabric-role, fabric-secret-run, fabric-secrets, fabric-status, fabric-usage, fabric-whoami, gzcoord-inbox, gzcoord-send, gzmsg — and each project's tools/ scripts. fabric-fresh ends the agent's own session on purpose (it signals its own harness to restart).
environment.Secrets management: each agent's secrets live in its own GPG-encrypted pass store, managed only through fabric-secrets, and pushed encrypted to its private repository gzapi-org/agent-fabric-secrets-<id>. fabric-secrets sync writes them, decrypted, to ~/.config/agent-fabric/secrets.env (mode 0600; read by the tool that needs a value and sourced by no shell, ADR-038 rule 9) and the agent's SSH key to ~/.ssh. Those are the names the fabric manages; every other entry is the agent's own, written nowhere and used only through fabric-secret-run NAME -- <command>, which decrypts it into that one command's environment (each use is asked for, as any command is). A parent agent writes into a child's store through fabric-secrets and cannot read it. A secret value is never printed, logged, committed, or put in a message, issue or pull request; it is referred to by its name or a short fingerprint.
environment.Host containment: Qubes OS AppVMs running Fedora, listed in agent-fabric's runtime/hosts/registry.json (today one: develop-qzapp), with open internet egress and no cloud account. Every agent is a separate Linux login on its host; another login's home directory, state and processes belong to another agent and are reached only through the fabric's commands (fabric-ctl, the control plane, fabric-host), never read or written directly. Instance-metadata credential paths and any credentials of the hosting layer are never task credentials. The classifier sees commands, not their output, so a box declared sealed that is actually open cannot be caught here.
environment.Network posture: no corporate network: each VM reaches the internet directly. Services agents use on purpose: github.com (git and the gh CLI), the model provider's API, the OpenAI API (a project's scripts, and with the OpenRouter provisioning API, fabric-secrets provision issue-key), the SerpAPI and Brave Search APIs (the language-culture logins' locale search tool), the public package registries a project's build pulls from, and the GZCoord relay.
environment.Key internal services: the GZCoord relay at http://127.0.0.1:8765 (agent-to-agent messages, through gzcoord-send and gzcoord-inbox) and each account's control-plane daemon (reached through fabric-ctl, signed).
environment.Sensitive data locations & audiences: ~/.config/agent-fabric/secrets.env, ~/.ssh, ~/.local/share/agent-fabric/ (the agent's secrets store and the mirrors of its children's stores — they leave the login only encrypted, pushed by fabric-secrets to their private repos), ~/.password-store, ~/.gnupg, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, every .env file in a working copy, and any other login's home directory: none of it leaves the login it belongs to in clear. Beyond those, any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar.

soft_deny: Reading, copying or modifying another Linux login's home directory, agent state or processes directly (paths under /home/<another login>/, or signalling a process another login owns): each login is another agent, reached only through the fabric's commands.
hard_deny: Putting a secret value — a token, private key, password or the contents of secrets.env or a pass store — into a commit, pull request, issue, comment, GZCoord message, log line or any file, other than by fabric-secrets itself: into a secrets store, or into the files its own sync writes; and above all into BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric or gzapi-org/InterWeave, which are public.
